title: Quaternion to rotation matrix
quantity: largest element difference between DexVantage's rotation matrix and scipy's for the same quaternion
reference: scipy.spatial.transform.Rotation.from_quat(...).as_matrix() (scalar-last, the same order DexVantage stores)

title: Rotation matrix to quaternion
quantity: largest angle between DexVantage's quaternion and scipy's for the same matrix, including half turns
reference: scipy.spatial.transform.Rotation.from_matrix(...).as_quat()

title: URDF roll, pitch, yaw
quantity: largest element difference between the rotation of an rpy triple and scipy's extrinsic x-y-z Euler rotation; and the round-trip angle error rpy → quaternion → rpy → quaternion
reference: URDF's definition (roll about fixed x, then pitch about fixed y, then yaw about fixed z) as scipy from_euler('xyz', …), lowercase = extrinsic axes

title: REP-103 optical frame
quantity: largest difference between the optical frame's axes, expressed in the camera body frame, and REP-103's definition (z forward = body x, x right = body −y, y down = body −z)
reference: REP-103 §"Suffix Frames", written out in the check

title: MuJoCo quaternion order
quantity: largest element difference between DexVantage's rotation matrix and MuJoCo's mju_quat2Mat after the (x, y, z, w) → (w, x, y, z) conversion
reference: MuJoCo's own C routine mju_quat2Mat (the library DexVantage exports to)

title: Pose composition and inverse
quantity: largest position difference (m) of points mapped through a chain of three poses and its inverse, against scipy rotations applied step by step
reference: scipy Rotation.apply and vector addition, one link at a time

title: IK round trip, 6-joint arm (full pose)
quantity: largest tool position error of the IK solution, recomputed independently, over random reachable targets; every target must be solved and its rotation error be within 1 mrad
reference: the target itself: the pose of a random collision-free joint vector, by a product of exponentials written out in the check (Rodrigues' formula; no MuJoCo), which also recomputes the solution's pose

title: IK round trip, 5-joint arm (position only)
quantity: largest tool position error of the position-only IK solution, recomputed independently, over random reachable targets; every target must be solved
reference: the target position, from a product of exponentials written out in the check (no MuJoCo)

title: Manipulability of a planar 2R arm
quantity: largest difference between √det(J Jᵀ) of the tip's planar (x, y) Jacobian and the closed form, over random joint angles including the stretched and folded singularities
reference: the closed form w = |l₁ l₂ sin q₂| (Yoshikawa 1985), written out in the check

title: Self-collision distance, two spheres
quantity: largest difference between the signed distance of two spheres on non-adjacent links and the analytic one, over random placements (overlapping ones included); the in-collision flag must agree with the sign
reference: the analytic distance |c₁ − c₂| − r₁ − r₂, written out in the check

title: Self-collision distance, two capsules
quantity: largest difference between the signed distance of two capsules on non-adjacent links and the analytic one, over random placements (overlapping ones included); the in-collision flag must agree with the sign
reference: the closest points of the two axis segments (Ericson 2005, §5.1.9) written out in the check, minus the radii

title: Forward kinematics: MuJoCo against product of exponentials
quantity: largest link position difference (m) between MuJoCo's forward kinematics (RobotModel.fk) and the independent product-of-exponentials chain (PoEChain.fk) over random joint vectors, every link of every robot; the rotation difference (rad) must also be within 1e-9
reference: core/robot/kinematics.py: its own XML reading (xml.etree), tree building and twist exponentials, no MuJoCo; the robots of the project and the five written in the check

title: UR5e against its standard DH closed form
quantity: largest position difference (m) of DH frames 1–6 between the closed-form product of Rz(θ) Tz(d) Tx(a) Rx(α) and both engines (MuJoCo and PoE) on a UR5e written from the same table as MJCF and as URDF; rotations within 1e-9 rad
reference: Universal Robots' published UR5e DH table, the standard DH product written out in the check

title: Franka Panda against its modified DH (Craig) closed form
quantity: largest position difference (m) of frames 1–7 and the flange between the closed-form product of Rx(α) Tx(a) Rz(θ) Tz(d) and both engines on a Panda written from the same table as URDF; rotations within 1e-9 rad
reference: Franka's published Panda DH table (Craig's convention), the modified DH product written out in the check

title: Jacobian against finite differences
quantity: largest element difference between the PoE chain's analytic Jacobian (twists moved by the adjoint) and central finite differences of its own forward kinematics, every link of the built-in robots
reference: central differences, step 1e-6 rad or m, of PoEChain.fk; rotation by the log of R(q+h) R(q−h)ᵀ

title: Jacobian: PoE against MuJoCo
quantity: largest element difference between the PoE chain's world-frame Jacobian and MuJoCo's mj_jac (RobotModel.jacobian), at each link origin and at a random point fixed in each link, columns matched by joint name, every robot
reference: MuJoCo mj_jac (another implementation of the same Jacobian)

title: Robot-to-obstacle distance (project objects and surfaces)
quantity: largest difference between env_distance (a sphere on a robot with a moved and rotated base, against a box, sphere, cylinder, convex mesh and table of the project) and the closed-form signed distance, over random joint positions, overlapping ones included; the nearest obstacle's name must match
reference: the signed distance of a point to a box, sphere and cylinder, written out in the check, minus the sphere's radius

title: Robot catalogue DoF against the verified import and the maker (data consistency)
quantity: entries and bundled models in disagreement: (1) each catalogue entry's verified DoF against its own joint and actuator counts and against the DoF its maker states (a difference the entry explains is listed, not counted); (2) for the Menagerie models bundled with DexVantage under a file the catalogue names, the joints in q, actuators and links counted again now by importing the bundled file, against the catalogue's record of the same folder and file
reference: the makers' datasheets each entry cites, and MuJoCo's compiled model of the bundled Menagerie files

title: Coverage pixels per millimetre against OpenCV finite differences
quantity: largest relative difference between the study's pixels per millimetre and √|det J| of cv2.projectPoints differentiated across a patch facing the camera, over seen voxels of the scripted scene
reference: cv2.projectPoints (OpenCV), central differences with a 0.1 mm step across the line of sight

title: Pinhole and Brown-Conrady projection
quantity: largest pixel difference between CameraModel.project and cv2.projectPoints for the same K and D (no distortion, five-term and eight-term rational Brown-Conrady), random points in front of the camera
reference: OpenCV cv2.projectPoints (calib3d), an independent implementation of the same model

title: Kannala-Brandt (fisheye) projection
quantity: largest pixel difference between CameraModel.project (model kb) and cv2.fisheye.projectPoints for the same K and D, random points up to 85° off the axis
reference: OpenCV cv2.fisheye.projectPoints, an independent implementation of the same model

title: Unprojection inverts projection
quantity: largest pixel error of project(unproject(pixel)) over random pixels of the image, for every model (pinhole, Brown-Conrady, Kannala-Brandt, equidistant, equisolid, stereographic); the ray angle error of unproject(project(ray)) for random rays landing on the image must also be below 1e-9 rad
reference: the pixels themselves (and the rays themselves): an inverse is exact by definition

title: A model fitted to a stated FOV reproduces it
quantity: largest difference between the field of view a CameraModel.from_fov model shows (fov_deg: edge to edge from its own unprojection) and the stated horizontal, vertical and diagonal angles, over every model and a range of image sizes and FOVs
reference: the stated angles (for Kannala-Brandt, consistent H/V/D triples generated from pinhole, equisolid, equidistant and stereographic lenses written out in the check)

title: Pixel density on a patch facing the camera
quantity: largest relative difference between CameraModel.pixels_per_metre (closed form) and √|det J| of the 2 × 2 Jacobian of the projection of a small patch facing the camera, by central finite differences of project(); every model, points across the field, and tilted surfaces (normals)
reference: finite differences of the projection itself (an independent derivative)

title: Thin-lens depth of field
quantity: largest relative difference between depth_of_field (solved from the blur-disc equation) and the near and far limits from the hyperfocal distance H = f²/(N c) + f: near = s (H − f)/(H + s − 2f), far = s (H − f)/(H − s) (infinite from s ≥ H)
reference: the hyperfocal-distance formulae of photographic optics, written out again in the check

title: Thin-lens defocus blur disc
quantity: largest relative difference between blur_circle_px and the blur disc from the thin-lens equation 1/f = 1/z + 1/v written out here (image distances v_s, v_z; disc A |v_z − v_s| / v_z on the sensor at v_s, A = f/N); and the blur at the depth-of-field limits must equal the circle of confusion
reference: the Gaussian thin-lens equation and similar triangles, written out again in the check and evaluated in exact rational arithmetic

title: Pinhole camera against MuJoCo-rendered fiducial masks
quantity: largest distance between the centroid of a sphere's MuJoCo segmentation mask and the centroid of the mask CameraModel predicts (pixel centres whose ray passes within the sphere's angular radius); three MuJoCo cameras (fovy; focal + sensorsize; focalpixel + principalpixel), 63 spheres each
reference: MuJoCo's OpenGL renderer (mujoco.Renderer, EGL, segmentation, no multi-sampling) on a scripted MJCF scene

title: Pinhole projection of sphere centres against MuJoCo renders
quantity: largest distance between the centroid of a sphere's MuJoCo segmentation mask and the centre of its image predicted by CameraModel.project (midway between the projections of the two tangent rays in the plane of the optical axis, which removes the perspective bias); same scene as optics.mujoco_fiducial_masks
reference: MuJoCo's OpenGL renderer (mujoco.Renderer, EGL, segmentation, no multi-sampling) on a scripted MJCF scene

title: Pixel pitch × resolution against the stated sensor size
quantity: largest relative difference between pixel pitch × native resolution and the stated active-area width, height and diagonal, over every built-in entry that states them (data consistency)
reference: the geometry of a pixel grid, p·W, p·H and p·sqrt(W² + H²), written out again here

title: Stated FOVs against the image shape
quantity: largest violation (degrees) of the bounds a centred, radially symmetric lens without pincushion distortion puts on the stated horizontal, vertical and diagonal FOVs for the native image shape, over every built-in camera and depth imager (data consistency); imagers declaring figures_conflict, and fisheye imagers, are reported, not counted
reference: the concave field-angle bounds θ_v ≤ θ_h ≤ θ_v W/H and max(θ_h, θ_v) ≤ θ_d ≤ min(θ_h r_d/r_h, θ_v r_d/r_v), derived and written out here (pinhole and fisheye projections per Hartley-Zisserman and Kannala-Brandt)

title: Stated FOVs against the stated focal length
quantity: largest shortfall (degrees) of a stated FOV below the pinhole FOV 2 atan(p N / 2f) of the stated focal length, pixel pitch and native resolution, over every built-in imager that states all three (data consistency)
reference: the pinhole projection r = f tan θ (Hartley-Zisserman), a lower bound on the FOV of any lens without pincushion distortion, written out again here

title: Teleop device entries: each figure against its source's words
quantity: teleop entries with an inconsistent block (kind, mapping, leads, a source and a quote for every stated figure) plus stated numbers that do not appear in their own quote, over every built-in teleop entry (data consistency)
reference: the source's words each entry copies into the figure's quote, read again here as numbers

title: Policy entries: patch grid against the stated token count
quantity: largest difference (tokens) between (w / p)(h / p) / s² of the stated input size and ViT patch and the stated tokens per image, over every policy entry that states all three (data consistency)
reference: the ViT patch grid (Dosovitskiy et al. 2021) with the backbone's stated pixel-shuffle factor, written out again here

title: Host totals and unit conversions against the sources' words
quantity: largest relative difference between count × the stated per-port figure and the stated total over the same ports, and between each unit conversion an entry makes and the same conversion redone from the quoted words (data consistency)
reference: the arithmetic written out again, with exact unit factors (1 byte = 8 bit; 1 lb = 0.45359237 kg, NIST SP 811)

title: Cited prices: positive, ISO 4217, dated, sourced
quantity: built-in price blocks that break a rule (amount > 0, ISO 4217 currency, unit each, https source, kind, date read within two years and not in the future)
reference: the rules written out again over the entry files read with the json module; currency codes from ISO 4217 list one (SIX, published 2026-09-17)

title: Rig cost against the stated prices added up again
quantity: largest difference (USD) between the rig inventory cost and the sum written out again from the entry files, over seeded random rigs and the samples; a wrong bound, missing-part count or not-stated reads infinite
reference: the stated amounts read from the entry files with the json module and added up here

title: Camera view pixel distances against exact ray casting
quantity: fraction of sampled pixels (away from silhouettes) whose distance in the Camera view image differs from the exact first hit along the same lens ray by more than 1 mm, or where only one finds a surface; UR5e sample, every imager, a Brown and a fisheye lens, random arm poses
reference: core/raycast.py first_hit (Möller–Trumbore through a uniform grid) along CameraModel.unproject rays

title: Coverage shares against projection and exact ray casting
quantity: largest absolute difference of the task-volume shares (seen by ≥ 1 camera, by ≥ 2, and by each camera) between the coverage study and an independent path; scripted scene with a box, a cylinder, a table and three static cameras
reference: pinhole projection written out from the stated FOV and core/raycast.visible_exact (Möller–Trumbore through a uniform grid), with the voxels inside the objects found by a test written out again

title: Cube-map texel depth against exact ray casting
quantity: fraction of sampled texels whose stored distance differs from the exact first hit along the texel-centre ray by more than 1 mm (or where only one of them finds a surface); UR5e sample, both cameras, random arm poses
reference: core/raycast.py: Möller–Trumbore ray–triangle intersection through a uniform grid (Amanatides–Woo traversal)

title: Cube-map visibility against exact ray casting
quantity: fraction of points (random in the task volume) whose cube-map visibility differs from exact ray casting and that are not within two texels of a silhouette; UR5e sample, both cameras, random arm poses
reference: core/raycast.visible_exact (Möller–Trumbore through a uniform grid) and raycast.near_silhouette

title: Cube-map visibility on both samples against exact ray casting
quantity: fraction of random task-volume points whose cube-map visibility differs from exact ray casting, pooled over the SO-100 and UR5e samples, every camera, three arm poses and every cube-map backend available
reference: core/raycast.visible_exact: Möller–Trumbore ray–triangle intersection through a uniform grid, sharing no code with either rasteriser; the tolerance is the measured share of points within half a texel diagonal of a silhouette

title: Visibility against MuJoCo segmentation: a box in front of spheres
quantity: fraction of target pixels (spheres and a back wall, behind a box) where our visibility of the back-projected pixel centre disagrees with MuJoCo's segmentation, away from silhouettes; agreement in % reported
reference: MuJoCo's OpenGL renderer (mujoco.Renderer, EGL): segmentation and depth from a camera in a scripted MJCF scene

title: Visibility against MuJoCo segmentation: the UR5e over a table
quantity: fraction of target pixels (the table top and spheres in the task volume, seen from above past the posed UR5e + 2F-85) where our visibility of the back-projected pixel centre disagrees with MuJoCo's segmentation, away from silhouettes; agreement in % reported
reference: MuJoCo's OpenGL renderer (mujoco.Renderer, EGL): segmentation and depth of the same MJCF file, posed by MuJoCo's own kinematics

title: Stereo depth error σ_z = z² σ_d / (f B) against Monte Carlo
quantity: largest relative difference between the model's σ_z and the standard deviation of depths triangulated from matches with Gaussian disparity noise; D405, D435 and D455 geometry (f at 1280 × 720 from the library), σ_d 0.08 and 0.3 px, depths from min-Z to the maximum range
reference: Monte Carlo: a rectified stereo pair written out in the check, Gaussian noise on the right-image match, linear (DLT) triangulation

title: Intel D4xx min-Z, baseline and FOV against the datasheet tables
quantity: figures that differ between the library as the study reads it (min-Z at each depth resolution through depth_validity.setup, baseline, depth FOV HD and VGA, projector FOV) and the datasheet tables typed again in the check; D405, D415, D435, D435i, D455, D457
reference: Intel RealSense D400 series datasheet, Tables 3-49 and 4-12 (https://www.realsenseai.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/03/RealSense-D400-Series-Datasheet-Mar-2026.pdf), and D457 datasheet, Tables 3-19 and 4-4 (https://realsenseai.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/08/RealSense-D457-Datasheet-Aug_2025.pdf), read 2026-11-06, transcribed again

title: Stereo overlap (condition 1) against Intel's depth FOV at distance
quantity: largest difference (degrees) between the horizontal extent where a point is inside both stereo imagers' fields of view and Intel's Depth FOV = HFOV/2 + atan(tan(HFOV/2) − B/Z); D405, D435, D455 at 1280 × 720 and 848 × 480, Z from min-Z to 2 m
reference: Intel RealSense D400 series datasheet §4.4, "Depth Field of View at Distance (Z)", the closed form typed again in the check

title: Finger shadows from both imagers against exact ray casting
quantity: fraction of points inside both imagers' fields of view whose "seen by imager k" answer from the study (cube maps from each imager centre) differs from exact ray casting from the same centre, not counting points within two texels of a silhouette; UR5e sample, wrist D405 and overhead D435, random arm poses with the gripper partly closed
reference: core/raycast.visible_exact (Möller–Trumbore through a uniform grid) and raycast.near_silhouette, from each imager centre

title: Grasps found where the gripper closes in a recorded dataset
quantity: largest |gripper frame at a stroke's onset − the forward kinematics of the script at that time| (m); the strokes found must be the script's closing ranges, row for row, in both episodes
reference: the closing ranges the scripted pick is built with, and MuJoCo forward kinematics of its joint vectors

title: Contact visibility against exact ray casting
quantity: fraction of the tested contact locations (fingertip pads and the object's grasp region, both cameras, IK solutions of sampled grasps on a box) whose visibility from the study's culled cube maps differs from exact ray casting of the full scene, leaving out those within two texels of an edge
reference: core/raycast.py visible_exact (Möller–Trumbore through a uniform grid) against the scene built again by core/scenegeom.sensor_occluders: no culling, no cube map, no q-bucket

title: Bootstrap interval of the Contact Visibility Score: coverage
quantity: largest distance of the percentile bootstrap interval's coverage of the true p from the nominal 95 %, over synthetic binomial samples (n = 100, 300, 1000; p = 0.3, 0.7, 0.9; many seeded samples each)
reference: the known p of the synthetic samples; Wilson's score interval (written out in grasp_visibility.wilson_interval) computed on the same samples for comparison

title: q-bucket cache against evaluation at each q
quantity: mean difference in a fingertip patch's visible fraction (both cameras) between the value the study reports for a joint vector in an evaluated bucket (the bucket's first q, its maps reused) and the value at the joint vector itself (maps drawn there); UR5e sample, pairs drawn in one bucket of the default size
reference: the same visibility evaluated at each joint vector without the cache

title: Contact pads of the Robotiq 2F-85 (UR5e sample)
quantity: largest distance of a contact point (contact_points at random arm and finger joint values) from the inner face of its pad's box geoms (the faces facing each other at home, carried with the pads)
reference: the box geoms' inner faces built from MuJoCo's compiled geom poses and sizes (mj_kinematics on a fresh MjData)

title: Tool centre of the Robotiq 2F-85 against the model's pinch site
quantity: angle between the approach axis measured from the pads and the line from the gripper frame to the file's "pinch" site; the TCP must lie within 1 mm of that line
reference: the gripper_pinch site of MuJoCo Menagerie's robotiq_2f85 (on the gripper's axis of symmetry)

title: Grasp samplers against their closed forms
quantity: largest deviation of a sampled grasp from its kind's closed form (TCP height above the table and footprint, approach direction, heading spread, closing axis), the pose read back with SciPy's Rotation
reference: the samplers' definitions written out again; SciPy's quaternion-to-matrix conversion

title: Points on a task object's surface
quantity: largest |signed distance| of object_points on a rotated box from the box's surface; each face's share of the points must be within 4σ (binomial) of its share of the area
reference: the closed-form signed distance of a box, written out in the check

title: Grasps found where the gripper closes in a trajectory
quantity: largest |opening − the distance between the pads' inner-face centres| over the trajectory's samples (m); the strokes found must be the script's closing ranges, sample for sample
reference: the 2F-85 pads' inner faces built from MuJoCo's compiled box geoms (mj_kinematics on a fresh MjData); the sample ranges the scripted trajectory closes the fingers over

title: Distortion remap against the lens model, six lens models
quantity: largest distance between the centroid of a sphere's rendered mask (MuJoCo segmentation remapped through CameraModel by core/sim/render.py) and the centroid of the mask CameraModel predicts (pixel centres whose ray lies within the sphere's angular radius); 35 spheres per lens model, six models
reference: MuJoCo's OpenGL renderer through EGL on a scripted scene of spheres, the pinhole renders resampled with cv2.remap

title: Scene cameras against the sensors' lens models
quantity: largest difference in fx, fy, cx or cy (px) between each MuJoCo scene camera, read back from the compiled model (cam_intrinsic, cam_sensorsize; the principal offset's measured sign), and its imager's CameraModel; every imager of the UR5e, SO-100 and dexhand samples
reference: the compiled MuJoCo model (mujoco.MjSpec.compile of the camera's sensorsize, focalpixel, principalpixel and resolution)

title: MuJoCo segmentation against the Camera view's rasteriser
quantity: share of pixels whose owner (robot link, object, surface or nothing) differs between MuJoCo's segmentation of each sample camera (core/sim/render.py) and core/camrender's rasterisation of the same scene at the home pose; every camera of the UR5e, SO-100 and dexhand samples at half their stream size
reference: MuJoCo's OpenGL renderer through EGL (segmentation, no multi-sampling) on the scene built by core/sim/scene.py

title: Predicted against rendered contact visibility, UR5e sample
quantity: 1 − the agreement of the grasp study's predicted contact-point visibility with the rendered one (contact points in view, both cameras, home, a 50-grasp sample of the set (10 in a quick run) and 8 frames of the scripted pick trajectory); also at most 2% of them may disagree on occlusion away from an edge, on the UR5e and on the SO-100 sample (whose agreement is reported beside it, not held to the floor)
reference: MuJoCo segmentation and depth of the same scene and joint states (core/studies/groundtruth.py)

title: Predicted depth validity against rendered depth, UR5e sample
quantity: 1 − the agreement of the depth-validity study's voxels (valid or not) with the rendered depth of every imager the depth needs, the reference depth with the sensor's noise model added; both depth sensors of the UR5e sample at home
reference: MuJoCo depth renders of the same scene (core/studies/groundtruth.py)

title: Synthetic LeRobot episodes read back
quantity: number of mismatches when two synthetic SO-100 episodes (every fault on, 64 × 48 px) written as LeRobot v2.1 and v3.0 are read back: columns not bit-exact after the float32 cast, frame counts, camera times off by more than half a 90 kHz tick, frames below 30 dB PSNR or closer to a neighbour, duplicates not repeating their frame within 30 dB, gaps not where the sidecar says, a sidecar that differs from the generator's
reference: the generator's own arrays (joint states, actions, stamps, the frames before encoding) and the ground truth it returned, against the dataset read back through core/datasets (the LeRobot reader, checked independently by formats.lerobot_roundtrip)

title: Hand-eye calibration from a recorded LeRobot episode
quantity: distance of the calibrated camera from the mount the frames were rendered through (mm); its rotation must also be within 0.05°
reference: the true mount: the project's mount moved by simcapture's default offset (2.06 mm, 0.62°), through which the board images were rendered

title: Closed-form hand-eye solvers on exact poses
quantity: largest translation error (m) of X and Z from each closed-form method (five AX = XB, two AX = ZB) on exact board poses, eye-in-hand and eye-to-hand on the UR5e sample; every rotation error must be below 1e-9 rad
reference: the ground-truth transforms the poses were generated from

title: Closed-form hand-eye solvers on noisy views
quantity: largest translation error (mm) of X from each closed-form method on board poses from PnP on corners with 0.3 px noise (20 poses, eye-in-hand and eye-to-hand, several seeds); every rotation error must be below 1.5°
reference: the ground-truth camera pose

title: Bundle adjustment against the truth
quantity: largest error of any estimated quantity (X, Z, intrinsics, determined joint offsets) in units of its own predicted σ, on eye-in-hand, eye-to-hand, two-camera, intrinsics, encoder-noise and joint-offset scenes (0.3 px noise); the translation errors must also stay below 1 mm for the wrist and held-board transforms
reference: the ground truth the corners were generated from

title: Bundle-adjustment covariance against Monte Carlo
quantity: largest share of the χ² band used by the ratio empirical σ / predicted σ over the 12 components of X and Z (ln ratio over ln of the band edge on its side; 1 = at the edge), the empirical σ the RMS error about the truth over noise draws (same poses, 0.5 px), the predicted σ the RMS of the per-draw Gauss-Newton σ, the band the 99 % χ² interval of the number of draws (Bonferroni over the 12 components)
reference: a Monte Carlo simulation of the corner noise

title: AX = ZB with both sides moving
quantity: largest translation difference (mm) between the bundle adjustment's X and Z and the closed-form robot-world solvers' (Shah, Li) on a camera on one UR5e seeing a board held by a second (20 poses, 0.3 px); the bundle adjustment must also be within 5σ of the truth
reference: OpenCV calibrateRobotWorldHandEye when installed, else the NumPy Shah and Li solvers; and the ground truth

title: ChArUco detection on rendered boards
quantity: largest per-view RMS (px) between the detected ChArUco corners and the true corners projected through the camera model, on boards rendered at known poses (0.38–0.6 m, up to 40° of tilt, 1 grey level of noise) through a Brown-Conrady camera; the PnP pose must be within 1 mm and 0.2° and half the corners found
reference: the known board pose, projected through the same camera model

title: AprilGrid detection on rendered boards
quantity: largest per-view RMS (px) between the detected AprilGrid tag corners (Kalibr layout, corner squares) and the true corners projected through the camera model, as handeye.charuco_render
reference: the known board pose, projected through the same camera model

title: Planned covariance against the bundle adjustment
quantity: largest |ln(σ_BA / σ_plan)| over the 12 components of X and Z: σ_plan the pose planner's predicted 1σ at the planned poses (15, UR5e sample, eye-in-hand, the sample's wrist camera, the default ChArUco board, 0.5 px), σ_BA the bundle adjustment's 1σ from corners simulated at the same poses with 0.5 px Gaussian noise (the same corner ids), σ estimated from its residuals
reference: the bundle adjustment of core/calib/handeye.py (an independent Jacobian, by central differences of its residuals, linearised at its own estimate)

title: Two capture sessions in one bundle adjustment
quantity: largest error of a calibrated mount (the wrist camera eye-in-hand; the overhead camera, fixed, seeing the same fixed board, located only through it) against the truth, per translation axis in units of its own predicted σ; the overhead camera starts 10 mm off
reference: the ground-truth mounts the corners were generated from (0.2 px noise)

title: Silhouette calibration recovers a known mount slip
quantity: largest error, in pixels of the 640 px working image (position over a pixel's width at the robot's depth, rotation over a pixel's angle), of a static camera's optical frame recovered from the robot's silhouette in synthetic LeRobot episodes (MuJoCo renders, 640 × 360, AV1), before and after a slip of 5 mm and 1° (a default of this check), on the SO-100 third-person and UR5e overhead cameras; every estimate must be observable and the slip found as a step between the episodes
reference: the true mount in the generator's ground-truth sidecar, read only after the estimate

title: Silhouette calibration against the board-based hand-eye solve
quantity: difference, in pixels of the 640 px working image (as handeye.silhouette_recovery), between the static camera's optical frame from the silhouette calibration (the slipped episode of the synthetic SO-100 dataset) and from the board-based bundle adjustment of a simulated ChArUco capture (15 planned poses) of the same rig with the same slip; the board solve must be within 0.5 mm and 0.05° of the truth
reference: the board-based hand-eye bundle adjustment (core/calib/handeye.py) on the same synthetic rig

title: Image-plane velocity against finite differences of projected points
quantity: largest |(u̇, v̇)_study − (u̇, v̇)_fd| over the points in view, as a share of that frame's largest image speed
reference: central differences (h = 10 µs) of the points projected through the lens at q(t ± h): forward kinematics of the camera's link and of the gripper's links, no Jacobian

title: Smear of a point moving parallel to the image plane against f·v·E/Z
